sourceArticle.title: Paper page - OmniRetrieval: Unified Retrieval across Heterogeneous Knowledge Sources
sourceArticle.author: Jinheon Baek ,

athenaOutput.directive: Architect a sovereign OmniRetrieval fabric to unify all internal and external knowledge sources into a single, queryable intelligence layer, making the Creative Liberation Engine omniscient.
athenaOutput.rationale: The Creative Liberation Engine's knowledge is currently fragmented across heterogeneous sources: strategic memos, code repositories, design files, pattern libraries, and operational logs. Inspired by the 'OmniRetrieval' paper, this initiative will create a unified natural-language interface to query all knowledge without erasing the unique structural advantages of each source. This will eliminate information silos, accelerate decision-making, and provide the foundational intelligence layer for all agents, directly fulfilling our constitutional mandate for automation and quality.

options.title: KEEPER Evolved: The Unified Knowledge Weaver
options.description: Upgrade the KEEPER agent's pattern library into a comprehensive OmniRetrieval engine for all internal Creative Liberation Engine knowledge. ARCHITECTURE: Implement a multi-modal retrieval pipeline with an LLM-based query router that dispatches requests to specialized retrievers for unstructured text (vector search), code (AST-aware search), and structured data. A synthesis layer will combine results into a single, coherent answer. DESIGN: Introduce a new 'OmniSearch' UI component, a powerful search bar that surfaces results on a 'knowledge canvas,' visually grouping related items like UI mockups next to their corresponding API specs. This interface will use glassmorphism and iconography to differentiate data sources.
options.tradeoffs: Focuses on internal knowledge first, potentially delaying integration with external tools. Requires significant upfront investment in building the core retrieval and synthesis layers.

options.title: The Agentic Librarian: Proactive Knowledge Synthesis
options.description: Frame OmniRetrieval not as a passive tool, but as an autonomous 'LIBRARIAN' agent that proactively synthesizes and surfaces context. ARCHITECTURE: The agent would listen to the Creative Liberation Engine's event bus. Upon detecting a new artifact (e.g., a git commit), it would use the OmniRetrieval backend to find related knowledge (design specs, user stories) and automatically append a summary to the new item. DESIGN: The UX is not a search bar but 'contextual intelligence' pods embedded throughout the UI. These non-intrusive sidebars would use subtle animations and muted tones to provide related information without disrupting workflow, appearing next to PRs, design files, or strategy docs.
options.tradeoffs: High potential for creating UI noise if not designed carefully. The value is dependent on the accuracy and relevance of the proactive suggestions, which can be difficult to tune.

options.title: The Sovereign Knowledge Graph: Weaving the Trinity's Web
options.description: Establish a canonical, queryable Knowledge Graph of the entire Creative Liberation Engine as the core retrieval source. ARCHITECTURE: Implement a sovereign graph database (e.g., Neo4j) and build continuous ETL pipelines to extract entities and relationships from all sources (code, design, strategy). The OmniRetrieval system becomes a natural language to graph-query (e.g., Cypher) translator. DESIGN: The primary interface would be a 3D, force-directed graph visualization tool. This allows users to navigate and explore the connections between strategy, design, and implementation visually, making complex dependencies intuitive and tangible.
options.tradeoffs: Highest architectural complexity and data modeling challenge. Requires a significant, long-term investment before providing broad utility. Data consistency across the graph is a major hurdle.

options.title: The External Bridge: OmniRetrieval as an Integration Hub
options.description: Position OmniRetrieval as the Creative Liberation Engine's interface to the outside world, unifying retrieval across external services like GitHub, Figma, and Notion. ARCHITECTURE: Develop a robust plugin architecture where each 'connector' handles a specific external API, translating queries and standardizing results. This centralizes external data access, reinforcing sovereignty. Agent SIGNAL would be heavily utilized. DESIGN: A 'Mission Control' dashboard with a central command bar for cross-service queries (e.g., 'Find user feedback in Intercom related to tickets in Linear'). Results would be aggregated into a single view, using source-service iconography within our unified design system.
options.tradeoffs: Creates dependencies on external APIs, which can be unstable or change without notice. Requires significant effort in security, authentication, and rate-limit management.

options.title: The Developer's Oracle: Code-Centric OmniRetrieval
options.description: Build a specialized OmniRetrieval system hyper-focused on developer and agent (BOLT) productivity. ARCHITECTURE: Develop deep, specialized retrievers for code (ASTs, semantic analysis), infrastructure-as-code definitions, OpenAPI specs, and performance monitoring data. A reasoning layer would connect these sources to answer complex questions like 'Why did latency for endpoint X spike after the last deployment?'. DESIGN: Primarily a CLI tool or deeply integrated IDE plugin. The UI would be text-based, information-dense, and optimized for expert users, using structured text output (tables, trees) over graphical interfaces to deliver answers with maximum speed and precision.
options.tradeoffs: Narrow focus provides immense value to a specific user group (developers) but neglects other domains like design and strategy. Risks creating another information silo if not eventually integrated into the broader system.
